proposed_value: Plasmid pool containing 1,000 enhancer and 1,000 promoter sequences in all pairwise combinations was transfected into K562 cells using a standard transfection protocol, with 50 million cells per biological replicate; transfection was performed using a transfection reagent (not explicitly named) and the hSTARR-seq_SCP1 vector with four polyA sequences upstream of the promoter position to prevent spurious transcription from the origin of replication. The library was delivered via lipid-based transfection, as implied by the use of standard STARR-seq protocols and the absence of electroporation or viral delivery mention.
rationale:
- The paper states that plasmid pools were transfected into K562 cells in 4 biological replicates of 50 million cells each (Passage 2), but does not name the transfection reagent.
- The use of the hSTARR-seq_SCP1 vector, designed to avoid spurious transcription, implies standard plasmid delivery methods (Passage 4).
- No mention of electroporation, viral vectors, or microinjection; thus, lipid-based transfection is inferred as the standard method for such assays in K562 cells.
